history.period: ancient/mythological; fort c. 15th century; ropeway inaugurated 1998
history.summary: Gabbar Hill is venerated as the mula pitha — the original seat of Goddess Amba, where (per the Tantra Chudamani) a part of Sati's heart fell. The hilltop shrine is a small cavern sanctum holding the goddess's charan-paduka (sacred footprints) and an eternal flame (akhand jyot) facing the Visa Yantra of the town temple. Legend says Rama and Lakshmana worshipped here and received the Ajay arrow used against Ravana. A parikrama path around the hill has replicas of all 51 Shakti Peethas. The 999-step climb can be skipped via the Shri Amba Devi Udan Khatola ropeway (1998). CSV town 'Ambaji' is the nearest town; the shrine is ~4.5 km southwest of it. Coordinates approximate (verify).

name: Gabbar Hill Temple
town_description: Ambaji is a major pilgrim town in Banaskantha district in northern Gujarat, on the Gujarat–Rajasthan border at the foothills of the Arasur (southern Aravalli) hills, near the traditional source of the Saraswati river. About 180 km from Ahmedabad and 45 km from Abu Road, it draws millions of pilgrims every year, especially on Purnima (full-moon) days, and is one of Gujarat's most important Shakti Peetha towns.
